title: Restricting a Kan fibration to component subcomplexes
statement: Use small simplicial sets, Kan complexes and Kan fibrations of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. For a simplicial set $Z$, define $\pi_0Z$ to be the quotient of its vertices by the equivalence relation generated by the endpoints of every edge. For a subset $S\subseteq\pi_0Z$, let $Z[S]$ be the simplicial subset consisting of the simplices all of whose vertices represent elements of $S$; call it a union of components. Let $p:X\to Y$ be a Kan fibration of small simplicial sets, let $S\subseteq\pi_0X$ and $R\subseteq\pi_0Y$, and suppose $(\pi_0p)(S)\subseteq R$. Then restriction gives a Kan fibration $p_{S,R}:X[S]\to Y[R]$. For every vertex $y$ of $Y[R]$, the strict fiber of $p_{S,R}$ is the simplicial subset $X_y\cap X[S]$ of $X_y=X\times_Y\Delta^0$, and this subset is a union of components of $X_y$. These fibers are Kan complexes. Moreover, if $Z$ is Kan then every $Z[S]$ is Kan. Empty subsets, empty simplicial sets and empty fibers are allowed; neither $X$ nor $Y$ is required to be Kan.

source.place: Rezk Section 12.2 and Lemma 13.9, printed pp.28,31-32: agent formulation of the component-subcomplex restriction argument implicit in passing from the degreewise homotopy monomorphism to its maps on strict mapping fibers. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-set assertion.

proof.text: First check the constructions from the definitions in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. If $z\in Z_n$ and $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, the vertex $j$ of $Z(\alpha)z$ is vertex $\alpha(j)$ of $z$. Thus the condition defining $Z[S]$ is preserved by every simplicial operator. For vertices $a\leq b$ of $z$, restriction along $[1]\to[n]$, $0\mapsto a$, $1\mapsto b$, is an edge between them, so all vertices of a simplex have the same component. A simplicial map sends edges to edges and therefore induces a map on the equivalence classes defining $\pi_0$. For $z\in X[S]$, each vertex of $p(z)$ has class in $(\pi_0p)(S)\subseteq R$. Consequently the degreewise restrictions of $p$ give a simplicial map $p_{S,R}:X[S]\to Y[R]$.

source.place: Construction of the component subcomplexes and restricted map; elementary argument by Q134, expanding the component restriction implicit in Section 12.2 and Lemma 13.9.

proof.text: Use the horn-lifting characterization of Kan fibrations in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Given a lifting square with top map $a:\Lambda_i^n\to X[S]$ and bottom map $b:\Delta^n\to Y[R]$, $n\geq1$, compose with the inclusions in $X,Y$ and use the hypothesis on $p$ to obtain a filler $h:\Delta^n\to X$. The horn has a vertex $v$: any included face has dimension $n-1\geq0$. Its image $h(v)=a(v)$ has component in $S$. Every other vertex $w$ is joined to $v$ by the image under $h$ of the edge of $\Delta^n$ with those endpoints; hence $[h(w)]=[h(v)]\in S$. Every simplex in the image of $h$ therefore has all vertices in $S$, so $h$ factors through $X[S]$. The two filler equations still hold in the subcomplexes, since their inclusions are degreewise injective. This supplies all horn lifts for $p_{S,R}$. In dimension one only one vertex lies in the horn; the filler edge supplies the other vertex and the same argument applies.

source.place: Horn lifting for the restricted map, including one-dimensional horns; elementary argument by Q134, expanding the component restriction implicit in Section 12.2 and Lemma 13.9.

proof.text: Fix a vertex $y$ of $Y[R]$, and denote its totally degenerate $n$-simplex by $y_n$. The degree-$n$ strict fiber of the restricted map consists exactly of $x\in X_n$ such that $p(x)=y_n$ and every vertex of $x$ has class in $S$. With the inherited operators these sets are $X_y\cap X[S]$. Explicitly, the pullback property is checked by sending any pair of compatible maps to its degreewise pairs $(x,*)$; uniqueness and compatibility with operators hold in every degree. To see the union-of-components assertion, let $j:X_y\to X$ be inclusion and put $T=(\pi_0j)^{-1}(S)\subseteq\pi_0X_y$. Edges of $X_y$ are edges of $X$, so $\pi_0j$ is well-defined. A simplex of $X_y$ has all its vertices in $T$ exactly when its vertices, regarded in $X$, have classes in $S$. Thus $X_y\cap X[S]=(X_y)[T]$, with no injectivity assertion about $\pi_0j$.

source.place: Degreewise identification of strict fibers and their component subsets; elementary argument by Q134, expanding the component restriction implicit in Section 12.2 and Lemma 13.9.

proof.text: The fibers in the preceding step are Kan without any fibrancy assumption on $Y$. Given a horn in $F=(p_{S,R})^{-1}(y)$, regard it as a horn in $X[S]$ and use as bottom simplex the constant simplex $\Delta^n\to Y[R]$ at $y$. Step 2 supplies a filler in $X[S]$ whose image is that constant simplex, so the filler lies in $F$. This proves the horn-filling condition, equivalently that $F\to\Delta^0$ is a Kan fibration and that $F$ is a Kan complex, using the fibrant-object convention of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. The identical argument with $p:X\to Y$ proves that the ambient strict fiber $X_y$ is Kan as well.

source.place: Horn filling of the strict fibers over a constant vertex; elementary argument by Q134, expanding the component restriction implicit in Section 12.2 and Lemma 13.9.

proof.text: Finally, if $Z$ is Kan, the unique map $Z\to\Delta^0$ is a Kan fibration by the fibrant-object convention of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Apply step 2 to this map, the subset $S\subseteq\pi_0Z$, and $R=\pi_0\Delta^0$. It gives a Kan fibration $Z[S]\to\Delta^0$, so $Z[S]$ is Kan. All constructions use subsets and degreewise maps, hence preserve smallness. If a component subset or fiber is empty, a horn cannot map into it because $n\geq1$ horns contain a vertex; its horn-filling condition is vacuous. An empty target has no vertices, so the fiber assertions in that case are vacuous too. Thus none of the empty cases requires an added hypothesis.

source.place: Kan component subcomplexes and the empty cases; elementary argument by Q134, expanding the component restriction implicit in Section 12.2 and Lemma 13.9.

lean.statement: theorem kan_component_restriction : (∀ (X Y : SSet.{u}) (p : X ⟶ Y) (S : Set (π₀ X)) (R : Set (π₀ Y)) (h : Set.MapsTo (mapπ₀ p) S R), Fibration p → Fibration (componentRestriction p S R h) ∧ ∀ y : (componentSubcomplex Y R).toSSet _⦋0⦌, (∃ e : pullback (componentRestriction p S R h) (const (X := Δ[0]) y) ≅ ((componentSubcomplex X S).preimage (pullback.fst p (const (X := Δ[0]) y.1))).toSSet, e.hom ≫ ((componentSubcomplex X S).preimage (pullback.fst p (const (X := Δ[0]) y.1))).ι ≫ pullback.fst p (const (X := Δ[0]) y.1) = pullback.fst (componentRestriction p S R h) (const (X := Δ[0]) y) ≫ (componentSubcomplex X S).ι) ∧ (componentSubcomplex X S).preimage (pullback.fst p (const (X := Δ[0]) y.1)) = componentSubcomplex (pullback p (const (X := Δ[0]) y.1)) ((mapπ₀ (pullback.fst p (const (X := Δ[0]) y.1))) ⁻¹' S) ∧ KanComplex (pullback (componentRestriction p S R h) (const (X := Δ[0]) y)) ∧ KanComplex ((componentSubcomplex X S).preimage (pullback.fst p (const (X := Δ[0]) y.1))).toSSet) ∧ (∀ (Z : SSet.{u}) (S : Set (π₀ Z)), KanComplex Z → KanComplex (componentSubcomplex Z S).toSSet)
